account: The Kangaroo Island Landscape Board in South Australia runs a program to eradicate feral cats from the 384 square kilometer Dudley Peninsula, with 200 fixed monitoring cameras. Board staff and their co-authors uploaded 101,586 images from 42 cameras, taken between 11 November 2020 and 9 September 2021 and already sorted by field staff, to eVorta, an Australian camera-trap classification service. eVorta correctly classified 482 of 492 cat images (97.9%) against 469 (95.3%) for staff, and missed one of 68 cat sequences where staff missed 11. It also produced 2,751 false cat alerts, against five by staff. Using program costs, the authors estimate that eVorta alone saved A$0.27 million (10%) over three years and that eVorta with 4G-connected cameras saved A$2.15 million (81%) and 115,838 kg of carbon emissions. Scientific Reports published the study on 24 June 2024. The cost figures come from a decision tool with program inputs and are estimates.
